newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex outlines crude, hydrcarbon reserves.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex outlines crude, hydrcarbon reserves.

text.p: Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Tuesday its proven crude reserves totaled 42.072 billion barrels as of Jan 1, 1997.
In an extended report of its 1996 activities, Pemex said its proven hydrocarbon crude-equivalent reserves totaled 60.9 billion barrels.

The 1997 crude figure showed a slight drop from the Jan 1, 1996, data of 42.146 billion barrels. The hydrocarbon figure was lower than the Jan 1, 1996 total of 62.058 billion barrels of crude equivalent.
Although Pemex has adopted a new methodology for calculating its crude and hydrocarbon resevres, these figures are based on the company's traditional way of calculating reserves.
The new methodology is more widely accepted internationally. The new way of calculating has only been applied in the offshore Campeche Sound region, the country's largest source of hydrocarbons.

Under the new calculation, Campeche hydrocarbon reserves totaled 17.1 billion barrels of crude equivalent, Pemex said on March 3. Using the traditional methodology, Campeche had proven hydrocarbon reserves 28.71 billion barrels of as Jan 1, 1996, which was updated to 27.923 billion as of Jan 1, 1997.
